prompts.overview:
Use case: stylized-concept. Deliverable: polished GAME VFX ART DIRECTION PREVIEW, an aspirational painted composite, not an actual engine screenshot or implementation claim.
Reference roles: image 1 is OUR GAME, use its six cute simple pixel slime identities, frontal sprite proportions and pale mint checker-tile floor. Its small weak dust and straight uniform purple lightning are the FAILED VFX being replaced: do not copy them. Images 2 and 3 are the user's collected lighting references: take the rich cool cyan versus warm amber color separation, selective glowing edges, bright cores with readable silhouettes, colored light affecting nearby ground; do not copy their scenery or characters. Image 4 is a lighting/impact reference only: layered immediate flash, directional sparks, illuminated contact point and darker supporting shapes. Do not include guns, zombies or realistic people.
Maintain the cute chunky pixel-art GAME characters, visible faces and clean small-scale readability. Build effects using artist-shaped tapered silhouettes and intentional asymmetry, bright white-hot small cores, saturated color body, darker contrasting outer edges, limited tasteful bloom and contact illumination. The main VFX shapes must read immediately when the preview is reduced in size. Bold generous effects about 2.5–3 slime body widths at the feet, large foreground arcs with smaller secondary fragments and a clear lingering afterglow. No evenly thin geometric lines, no stock radial starburst on every element, no busy magical text, no rune circle, no hologram circuitry, no glossy toy renders, no giant overexposed white blob, no cinematic scenery redesign. The floor stays the existing LIGHT mint tile floor. No health bars or gameplay HUD.
Composition: landscape 3 columns by 2 rows comparison board, exactly SIX equally sized panels, subtle gutters, each cell showing ONE slime at the peak of its exaggerated landing effect on the same floor at the same camera view and scale. No massive poster title. Small clear Korean labels only: top row "불", "물", "땅"; bottom row "바람", "번개", "무속성".
FIRE: orange slime with flame ornament; landing blossoms into sweeping orange-red flame petals around its feet, yellow-white contact center, upward tapered sparks and a low rolling orange heat ring, char face clearly visible.
WATER: cyan slime with wave ornament; a large sculpted crown of splash and two thick curling aqua ribbons spread sideways, brilliant white foam edges, translucent blue interior, large round droplets with short trails, widening water ripples.
EARTH: sandy tan slime with a rock ornament; chunky angular stone shards tilt outward around a powerful ochre ground impact, thick rolling tan dust lobes with darker undersides, a few golden contact highlights, weight and texture rather than electric-looking glow.
WIND: pale mint slime with a dark teal curl ornament; two or three wide beautifully tapered mint-white crescent ribbons coil around the feet and sweep out, dark teal edges to read against the pale floor, subtle curled wisps and a few small leafy flecks.
LIGHTNING: yellow slime with purple bolt ornament; beautiful irregular hand-drawn branching electricity spreads ALONG THE FLOOR, dramatic variation in thickness, small white-hot core inside broad golden strokes with violet rim/afterglow, thick tapered roots and fine branching ends, a concentrated moving highlight along one branch; a few short low arcs at the contact point. NOT a floating beam or a spiderweb of thin purple straight segments.
NEUTRAL: green slime without element ornament; a broad pillowy cream dust burst with rolling smoky lobes and darker sage-tan underside, short curved white impact strokes, several visible pebble flecks, soft lingering dust. This must be as clearly visible and art-directed as the elemental versions without pretending to be elemental magic.
The six slimes remain recognizable as the source game's characters. Effects should have distinctly different materials and motion language rather than six recolors of a common explosion.

Composition: widescreen FOUR-panel left-to-right storyboard of ONLY the yellow lightning slime with its purple bolt ornament, exactly same camera, floor, character scale and fixed landing center in every panel. Minimal Korean captions and illustrative timing: "착지 섬광 · 0.00초", "번개 확산 · 0.12초", "빛의 질주 · 0.28초", "잔광 소멸 · 0.65초". These timings are conceptual.
Artist-designed ground lightning with beautiful irregular branching taper, white-hot thin heart, thick saturated gold stroke and violet outer halo; angular but not a computer schematic. Ground footprint is about THREE slime widths; face remains visible. Color illumination on the mint tiles makes the electricity feel attached to the world.
Panel 1: visible exaggerated squash pose, tight explosive white-gold contact flash beneath the slime, short thick energetic hooks beginning to reach out, violet darker outer accents.
Panel 2: branches rapidly unfurl ALONG THE FLOOR in an irregular oval footprint, thick roots and tapered small ends, little low electric arcs, strong gold/violet contrast. No vertical lightning pillar.
Panel 3: the same footprint clearly recognizable with a brilliantly highlighted streak traveling down selected branches from center toward tips; remaining branches are darker violet/gold. An energetic brief double-exposure afterimage makes motion obvious in this still frame, without copying the slime face.
Panel 4: main impact gone, elegant broken violet-gold branch afterimages and a few tiny sparks break apart at the outer tips, ground light fades, slime recovers its round shape. Enough residual shape remains to understand the dissipation.
Make each phase visually intentional; do not merely duplicate a purple zigzag with changed opacity. No UI, no black background, no alien emblem, no magic circles. Production-quality pixel/sprite compatible VFX art, not a scientific diagram.
